chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Muhammad al-Wabishi and Ibrahim ibn Mihran, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) led the people in the morning prayer, so he looked at a youth in the mosque; he was trembling and bowing his head, his complexion was yellowish, his body had become thin, and his eyes were sunken in his head.
So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to him: 'How is your morning, O so-and-so?' He said: 'I woke in the morning, O Messenger of Allah, with conviction (yaqeen).'
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was astonished by his words and said: 'Indeed, for every conviction there is a reality; so what is the reality of your conviction?'

He said: 'My conviction, O Messenger of Allah, is that which grieved me, kept me awake at night, and made my throat thirsty. My soul turned away from the world and what is in it, to the extent that it is as if I am looking at the Throne of my Lord, and the Reckoning has been established, and the creatures have been gathered for that, and I am among them.'

And it is as if I am looking at the people of Paradise, enjoying themselves in Paradise, getting to know one another, and reclining on raised couches; and it is as if I am looking at the people of Hell, and they are being punished in it, shrieking.
And it is as if I am now hearing the sighing of the Fire circulating in my ears.

So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to his companions: 'This is a servant whose heart Allah has illuminated with faith.' Then he said to him: 'Stick to what you are upon.'
The youth said: 'Supplicate to Allah for me, O Messenger of Allah, that I may be granted martyrship with you.'

So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) supplicated for him, and it was not long before he went out in one of the military expeditions of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and he was martyred after nine men, and he was the tenth.
ai.seo_question: What is the reality of conviction (yaqeen) in Shia tradition and how does it lead to martyrship?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the Shia concept of 'Yaqeen' as a transformative, visionary state where the believer perceives the Hereafter with such clarity that worldly attachments fade, a phenomenon often linked to the spiritual illumination (noor) of the heart. The Prophet’s affirmation of this state and his specific prayer for martyrship highlight the high status of steadfast conviction in achieving ultimate success, reinforcing the theological link between inner certainty and outward sacrifice.
